answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing and stated: (1) a ticket building a red-first proof declares the red teeth under its own id in that proof's PROVES; that is what makes the proof red-first for it, so D3's case (a building ticket carries its own red) survives. (2) proof_coverage.declared(proof) is the reader of PROVES (it already reads test_rehearsal.py's declared teeth by ticket id), so carried() needs no new parser. (3) A red item whose tooth is '*' (the proof printed no tooth) is carried by any open bounding ticket that declares teeth in that proof, and by none that declares nothing. (4) fixes stays a per-proof carry, which is 207c4074b3d5 D1 ('a second tooth reding on a proof an open ticket already fixes is the same repair'). (5) The carry only reads tickets not at a terminal state, unchanged.
answers.builder_check: Questions a Haiku builder would need answered, answered here. Where? red_tickets.py carried() (line 156) and ticket_what_is_new (line 405, the dedupe loop that checks item['path'] in fixes or bounds). What does carried() return now? (fixes: set of paths, bound_keys: set of red keys 'red:<rel>::<tooth>' plus 'red:<rel>::*' when the bounding ticket declares any tooth in rel). How are declared teeth read? cairn.tools.proof_coverage.declared(<abs proof path>) returns {ticket_id: {n: tooth}}; take the bounding ticket's id. How is a partly carried item cast? drop the carried keys from item['keys']; skip the item when none remain; the cast's measured 'keys ...' lists only the remainder. Callers of carried()? grep before changing the return; keep the tuple arity. 207c's tooth 3: give its fixture's open ticket a PROVES-declared tooth in RED so it still casts nothing, and leave its unbound twin as is. Proof timeout under 300s; fixture commons as 207c's _world does.
